$comment: Budgets for test/perf/run.ts (npm run perf). Times are milliseconds on the reference device: the reference machine with
Chromium's CPU throttled `rate` times. Another machine runs the calibration workload first and throttles by
rate x reference.calibrationMs / its own calibration, so it emulates the same device and the same budgets apply.
`max`, `min` or `equals` fail the run when `gate` is not false. `target` is the plan's number (section 8.7 or principle 5),
shown as met or not met and never failing the run. `why` says how each number was derived; measured values are
from docs/performance.md: six full runs on the reference machine, each the median of 11 loads, 5 scripted visits, 2 churn windows, 1 idle minute and 4 simulated days.

reference.machine: Apple M3 Max (one performance core), macOS, Chromium 153

startup.article.ms.why: Measured 4.7 ms (27.5-31.4 ms before the time zone was read only on a matching screen, 3 October). 12 ms leaves about 2.5x headroom for hardware the calibration evens out imperfectly; the plan's 2 ms is not met, with no single hot spot left.

startup.feed.ms.why: As for the article page; start-up does not depend on the page (measured 4.9 ms).

startup.cold.ms.why: The first document of a newly launched browser: measured 4.9 ms, no worse than warm. Same ceiling.

firstSecond.article.ms.why: Library time in the second after start-up on a page that does not change: measured 0.

firstSecond.feed.ms.why: The same on the churning feed: observer callbacks and debounced marker reads, measured 2.1-2.5 ms; about 3x headroom.

startup.article.longTasks.why: Plan 8.7: no long tasks. Measured 0 of 11 loads (the load task 29 ms) since the time zone is read only on a matching screen; before, 4 to 11 of 11.

startup.feed.longTasks.why: As for the article page: 0 of 11.

lcp.article.added.why: Measured +4 ms; on a page this light the deferred script runs before the first paint, so the paint waits for start-up. 16 ms is one frame. Before the lazy time zone it was +28 to +36 ms.

lcp.feed.added.why: Measured -8 to 0 ms: the feed paints after its own parsing. One frame, as for the article.

cls.article.added.why: The library never changes layout: no DOM writes, no styles.

dom.article.writes.why: Plan 8.7: no DOM writes except the opt-in form field. Every DOM change from the start of the document, compared with the same page without the library (less the script element itself).

network.requests.why: Plan 8.7 and principle 5: no network request. Every request in every load beyond the page, the script and the page's image.

render.blocking.why: The script tag (defer) is reported by Chromium as non_blocking in every load.

input.article.median.why: Library time inside each trusted pointerdown, keydown, input and wheel dispatch: measured 0.015-0.024 ms (a visibility check and a timestamp); 4x headroom.

input.feed.median.why: Measured 0.010-0.018 ms on the 10,000-node feed; 5x headroom.

input.article.p95.why: The 95th percentile is the marker read that a pointerdown or keydown triggers at most every 300 ms: measured 0.56-0.71 ms (max 0.85); about 3x headroom.

input.feed.p95.why: Measured 0.63-0.77 ms (max 0.8): the marker read scans the whole document for one attribute, so it grows with the DOM.

inp.article.added.why: Measured 0 in every run (48 to 48 ms). Event Timing rounds durations to 8 ms, so one step either way is noise; two steps fail.

inp.feed.added.why: Measured 0 in every run (48-56 ms both ways); as for the article page.

churn.ms.why: Library time per second while the feed adds and removes a <body> child every frame: measured 1.3-2.45 ms/s (60 observer callbacks a second and about 4 marker reads of 0.26-0.36 ms on 10,000 nodes); about 2.5x headroom over the worst run.

churn.timers.why: The 250 ms debounce allows 4 reads a second, plus the 5 s pass and the slow sample in the window: measured 4.05-4.1. More means the debounce broke.

day.callbacks.why: One interval callback every 5 s for 24 hours. A faster slow sample, or a second interval, fails this.

day.retained.why: Heap the library holds once started, after a collection: measured 105-106 KB (code, the registry tables, closures); 1.5x headroom.

day.firstDays.why: Heap growth over the first two simulated days beyond the page's own: measured 12.3-12.8 KB, the JIT tiering up the interval callback.

day.steady.why: Growth on day four beyond the page's own: measured 1.2 KB (0 in a six-day exploratory run). Anything per callback that is kept would show here as about 17,000 times its size.

day.listeners.why: The document keeps the same listeners all day.

idle.visible.timers.why: Expected 7 in 30 s: the passes at 1.5 s and 5 s and the slow sample every 5 s. Measured 7.

idle.visible.queries.why: 8 DOM queries per marker read (one attribute query, the icon links, six ids) times 7 reads, measured 56; one read of slack.

idle.visible.ms.why: Measured 1.8-3.7 ms in 30 s. Single idle wake-ups are noisy (some take 1-2 ms), hence the loose ceiling; the counts are the tight checks.

idle.visible.perCall.why: Median callback measured 0.09-0.36 ms between runs (idle wake-ups are noisy); a marker read on this page is about 0.1 ms.

idle.hidden.timers.why: The slow sample's interval still fires while hidden (6 in 30 s) and returns after one visibility check.

idle.hidden.queries.why: Plan 4.8: the slow sample runs only while visible. No DOM query in 30 s hidden.

idle.hidden.ms.why: Recorded, not gated. Six callbacks that each return after one visibility check measured 3.8-13.2 ms in all (one took 6.1 ms): a hidden renderer runs at low priority and the first callback after hiding can include a collection the browser schedules, so the time is the environment's. The query count and the callback count are the checks.

idle.hidden.perCall.why: Recorded, not gated: median callback measured 0.38-0.66 ms between runs for the same no-op, for the reasons above.

idle.requests.why: No request in a minute left open, visible or hidden.

idle.storage.why: Principle 5: no cookie, no storage. localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, IndexedDB and Cache Storage after a minute.
